name: Moroccan Beef and Olive Tagine
description: A slow-braised Moroccan beef and olive tagine with preserved lemon, saffron, and potato wedges. Halal, no alcohol, built on classical braising technique.
keywords: halal tagine, beef olive tagine, preserved lemon, saffron, halal french cooking, Moroccan braise
recipeIngredient: 500 g lean halal beef, cut into 4 cm cubes
700 g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
1 large handful green or red olives
1/2 preserved lemon, cut into long quarters
1 small handful flat-leaf parsley or coriander

recipeInstructions.name: Coat beef with spices
recipeInstructions.text: In a wide, heavy-bottomed pot, combine the beef cubes, sliced onion, grated garlic, ginger, turmeric, black pepper, salt, chilli if using, and olive oil. Mix until the beef is thoroughly coated.

recipeInstructions.name: Sweat aromatics
recipeInstructions.text: Place over medium heat and cook, stirring occasionally, for about eight minutes until the onion softens and the spices bloom in the oil.

recipeInstructions.name: Add water and saffron
recipeInstructions.text: Pour in 700 ml water and crumble in the saffron. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cover with a lid slightly ajar.

recipeInstructions.name: Add potatoes
recipeInstructions.text: Arrange potato wedges over and around the beef. Replace the lid, still ajar, and simmer for 20 more minutes.

recipeInstructions.name: Check and reduce if needed
recipeInstructions.text: Test the potatoes with a paring knife. If the sauce is very thin, remove the lid and increase heat for five minutes to reduce.

recipeInstructions.name: Add preserved lemon and olives
recipeInstructions.text: Lay the preserved lemon quarters and olives over the top. Replace the lid for three to four minutes.

recipeInstructions.name: Finish and serve
recipeInstructions.text: Scatter parsley or coriander over the top and serve directly from the pot with couscous or bread.
